questions.text: When did Henry VIII die?

questions.text: When did Ireland become unified with England, Wales and Scotland?
questions.explanation: In 1801, Ireland became unified with England, Scotland and Wales after the Act of Union of 1800. This created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

questions.explanation: The devolved administrations each have their own civil service.

questions.text: On Remembrance Day, there is a two-minute silence at 11 AM to commemorate those who died fighting during the First World War.
questions.explanation: On Remembrance Day at 11.00 am there is a two-minute silence and wreaths are laid at the Cenotaph in Whitehall, London.

questions.text: What is the distance between the north coast of Scotland and the south-west corner of England?
questions.explanation: In the UK, the longest distance on the mainland is from John O’Groats on the north coast of Scotland to Land’s End in the south-west corner of England. It is about870 miles(approximately 1,400 kilometres).

questions.text: Who was Henry Purcell?
questions.explanation: Henry Purcell (1659-95) wasthe organist at Westminster Abbey. He wrote church music, operas and other pieces, and developed a British style distinct from that elsewhere in Europe.

questions.text: How are life peers appointed?
questions.explanation: Life peers are appointedby the monarch on the advice of the Prime Minister.

options.text: By the monarch on the advice of the Prime Minister
By the Prime Minister on the advice of the King

questions.text: Where is the Giant’s Causeway located?
questions.explanation: The Giant’s Causeway is locatedon the north-east coast of Northern Ireland.

questions.text: Who proposed that enemy aircrafts could be detected by radio waves and is responsible for the development of the radar?
questions.explanation: The radar was developed by ScotsmanSir Robert Watson-Watt(1892-1973), who proposed that enemy aircraft could be detected by radio waves. The first successful radar test took place in 1935.

questions.text: During Halloween people carve lanterns out of ______ and put a candle inside of them.

questions.text: In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, if an accused person is aged 18, the case will be heard in a Youth Court:
questions.explanation: In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, if an accused person isaged 10 to 17, the case is normally heard in a Youth Court in front of up to three specially trained magistrates or a District Judge.
